papers.title: A Model-Driven Approach for Design and Generation of Collaborative Cross-platform Graphical Editors in Engineering Education
papers.abstract: This work introduces a Model-Driven Development (MDD) approach for the design and automatic generation of collaborative cross-platform and multitouch graphical editors tailored to engineering education. The proposed method facilitates the creation of customizable graphical editors, aiming to balance ease of use with the flexibility afforded by model-based design. While a foundational understanding of modelling tools is advantageous during the initial development phase, the resulting editors provides an inclusive user experience across diverse devices and operating environments. A preliminary evaluation involving university professors has been conducted to assess the effectiveness of the approach. The results underscore several strengths, notably the high degree of automation and the support for collaborative learning scenarios. Nonetheless, the evaluation also revealed limitations, including usability issues and dependence on specific integrated development environments (e.g., Eclipse). Overall, the proposed approach contributes to the advancement of scalable and innovative modelling tools in engineering education, fostering active learning and enhanced conceptual comprehension of modelling languages.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文讨论工程教育中图形编辑器的模型驱动生成，与FEA代理建模、仿真采样效率或植入物生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper presents an MDD tooling approach for educational graphical editors and contains no surrogate modeling, no FEA, no uncertainty quantification, and no biomechanics or implant design context.

summary_en.motivation: The work aims to simplify the creation of customizable collaborative graphical editors for engineering education.
summary_en.method: A model-driven development approach is used to automatically generate cross-platform multitouch editors from models.
summary_en.result: A preliminary professor-based evaluation indicates strong automation and collaborative support but reveals usability and IDE-dependence limitations.
summary_en.validation: Validation relies on a preliminary qualitative evaluation with university professors rather than quantitative or simulation-based testing.
